site.description: Alan Xu is an interactive developer building motion-led digital work.
site.aboutText: ALAN XU BUILDS MOTION-LED DIGITAL EXPERIENCES, INTERACTIVE TOOLS, AND WEB SYSTEMS WITH A FOCUS ON RHYTHM, CLARITY, AND DETAIL.

title: BLADE
RUNNER
projects.description: Neon fog, synthetic memory, and monumental color fields shaped as a slow cinematic system.
frames: NEON
Electric city haze, amber interiors, and hard silhouettes.
MEMORY
Faces and fragments staged like evidence from another life.
SCALE
Brutalist spaces turn the human figure into a small signal.
FUTURE
A noir rhythm built from silence, weather, and artificial light.

chapters.title: STRIKE
chapters.summary: Holographic grid lines, flying cars, gunfire, neon bodies, and the red title card land as one metallic impact.

chapters.title: WALLACE
chapters.summary: A fog-choked pyramid, glass tanks, and Wallace's birth ritual frame replicants as a disposable workforce.

chapters.title: ORDER
chapters.summary: Joshi's warning about walls and war plays over rain, police vehicles, blood, and neon signs in the night city.

chapters.title: DESERT
chapters.summary: The trailer shifts to orange dust, buried statues, and Deckard's guarded encounter with K inside a sun-bleached ruin.

chapters.title: CHAOS
chapters.summary: Storm flight, snow markets, explosions, flipped cars, fire, and magenta club gunfire push the cut into action velocity.

chapters.title: JOI
chapters.summary: A glitching Joi screen, a sunlit forest, Luv's advance, and Joi's intimate words slow the trailer into emotional resolve.

chapters.title: TITLE
chapters.summary: K lifts his gaze before the final Blade Runner 2049 title, credits, IMAX card, hashtag, and release date burn out.

title: DUNE
DESERT
projects.description: Desert scale, ritual architecture, and slow pressure arranged as a vast visual language.
frames: SAND
A restrained palette turns the landscape into a graphic field.
POWER
Ceremony, armor, and architecture carry the political weight.
VISION
Dream images arrive as fragments before the world explains them.
SCALE
Wide frames use distance and silence to make the myth feel physical.

title: GRAND
HOTEL
projects.description: Symmetry, powder color, and theatrical blocking make every frame read like a designed object.
frames: PALETTE
Pink facades, red uniforms, and icy blues build instant recognition.
ORDER
Centered compositions make motion feel like choreography.
CAST
Faces and costumes become a dense editorial system.
PACE
Fast cuts stay legible because every frame has strict geometry.

title: LIGHT
HOUSE
projects.description: A square, storm-heavy image world where grain, faces, and darkness do most of the speaking.
frames: GRAIN
Heavy texture makes the image feel carved instead of photographed.
FACES
Portraits hold pressure through stillness and extreme contrast.
STORM
Weather becomes a moving wall around the characters.
RITUAL
The trailer builds dread through repetition, sound, and hard cuts.

title: MOOD
LOVE
projects.description: Red corridors, green shadows, and close textures turn restraint into pure visual memory.
frames: COLOR
Red fabric, green rooms, and warm practical light carry emotion.
DISTANCE
Characters are framed through doors, walls, and partial reflections.
RHYTHM
Slow motion and repeated passages create a private pulse.
MEMORY
The image feels less like plot and more like something remembered.

title: FURY
ROAD
projects.description: Orange dust, blue night, chrome machinery, and centered action built for maximum velocity.
frames: DUST
The palette is brutal and simple: heat, metal, sky, skin.
MACHINE
Vehicles read like characters because their shapes are so specific.
CENTER
Action remains readable by locking the eye to the middle of frame.
IMPACT
Cuts, crashes, and scale build a graphic rhythm of acceleration.

title: ODYSSEY
projects.description: Pure geometry, human scale, and cosmic silence form one of cinema's clearest visual systems.
frames: VOID
Black space and white interiors make each object feel absolute.
GEOMETRY
Circles, corridors, and screens turn design into narrative.
HUMAN
Small gestures sit against impossible technological calm.
COSMIC
The trailer suggests awe through scale more than exposition.

title: POOR
THINGS
projects.description: A surreal color machine of distorted rooms, theatrical bodies, and strange comic luxury.
frames: WORLD
Rooms bend toward fantasy while staying rich in tactile detail.
COLOR
Turquoise, crimson, cream, and black keep the image alive.
BODY
Performance and costume create a visual language of discovery.
STRANGE
The trailer's rhythm turns spectacle into a designed curiosity.
